summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for a flare characterized by epigastric pain radiating to the back and nausea. She had normal lipase and liver enzymes but a clinical picture consistent with her typical flares, managed with IV hydromorphone and continued TPN. Pain gradually improved, allowing transition to oral analgesics and a soft diet. She also had acute pharyngitis, which resolved during the stay. Her iron deficiency anemia and depression were managed with ongoing oral supplementation and psychiatric medications. She was discharged home with service, tolerating oral intake, pain controlled on outpatient regimen, and plans for close GI follow-up and weekly lab monitoring. A chest X-ray showed stable PICC line position and a nonspecific diaphragmatic bulge, likely related to splenic position, with no intervention required.
